newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch receiver aims to sell Shipmair by July 1.
newsitem.headline: Dutch receiver aims to sell Shipmair by July 1.

text.p: ROTTERDAM, June 20 (Reuter) The official receiver of Shipmair, the bankrupt Rotterdam-based dry cargo charterer, said on Friday he is aiming to have sold the company by July 1 - following the failure of legal action by two shareholders to prevent the sale.
Receiver, John Wolfs of the company Houthoff, is inviting further bids for the company in addition to the four he has already received. He is aiming to call an end to bidding by late Monday, June 23.

The two other shareholders in International Bulk Handling Services NV (IBHS), which is also one third owned by Multimare - the parent company of Shipmair, had tried to prevent the sale of Shipmair. Wijsmuller and HES Beheer had placed an injunction against Wolfs to stop the sale.

The two claimed that shares in another company, Flutrans, should be transferred to them following the failure of Shipmair. Shipmair's Brazilian sister company, Shidobra (which is 100 percent owned by Shipmair) holds a 40 percent stake in Flutrans as do Brazilian interests, with the remaining 20 percent owned by IBHS.
However, a Rotterdam court ruled this week that Flutrans shares should not automatically be transferred to the two IBHS shareholders.
The receiver did not have to abide by the Voting Trust Agreement which had been formed previously by the shareholders of Flutrans, the court ruled.
The unsuccessful court action has enabled Wolfs to go ahead with the sale of Shipmair and its Brazilian arm Shidobra.
Wolfs said he felt that more prospective buyers may come forward after the court ruling. "There were indications that bidders were hesitant because of the South American conflict."
He is already negotiating with the four firms to have expressed an interest.

It could be possible that the two IBHS shareholders might chose to buy into Shipmair or Shidobra, he added. "As long as it is in the interest of the creditors, we do not mind which company buys them," said Wolfs.
Shipmair specialised in the agribulk trade between Europe and Latin America. The company went bankrupt on Friday, May 23, collapsing with debts totalling $3.7 million.
